quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to driving a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
A motorcycle is easier to see than a car.
You should pass on the shoulder instead of the main road.
You must make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller than cars. They can easily disappear into a driver's blind spot. Drivers may not notice you even if they look.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a good view of the shoulder.
Make it hard to see road hazards.
Allow others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and lets them see you. Do not ride in another driver's blind spot for long periods.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers can see you as easily as they see cars.
Assume other drivers cannot see you.
Not worry about whether other drivers see you.
Ride aggressively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer and smaller lights than other vehicles. They are hard to see. Ride safely and assume others cannot see you.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders who wear helmets.

options.text: Half as likely
Twice as likely
Three times as likely
Just as likely

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs show road rules like speed limits. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: In group riding, what does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Danger ahead.
Stop.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Hand signals are important for group riding. When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with palm facing back, the group should stop.

questions.question: Over-the-counter drugs like cold tablets:

options.text: Can affect your ability to safely ride.
Usually will not affect your riding ability.
Do not affect your riding ability.
Are always safe to take before riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to safely ride.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medications, can affect your ability to ride safely. Learn about side effects before taking any drug and riding.

questions.question: If you are carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean with you when you lean.
Hold onto the motorcycle seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with you when you lean.
questions.explanation: A passenger should lean with you through turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control, and hold onto the passenger handholds, your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What best protects your eyes from wind?

options.text: Eyeglasses
Sunglasses
A windshield
Goggles

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Prevent other drivers from sharing your lane.
Give you a nice view of scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your intentions from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent other drivers from sharing your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position keeps you safe in many ways. It keeps you out of blind spots, helps you see and be seen, helps you avoid road hazards, helps you avoid wind from other vehicles, and gives you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It guarantees the other driver will yield to you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not mean the driver will yield to you.
It means the driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with another driver means they will give you the right-of-way. Do not rely on it for safety.

questions.question: What is true about approved motorcycle helmets?

options.text: They can limit the rider's view.
They allow the rider to see well to the sides.
They are dangerous to wear.
You do not have to wear one if it limits your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They allow the rider to see well to the sides.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets do not limit your vision. They let you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It protects your whole face.
It protects less than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield.

questions.question: What should you do to help drivers merge from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Move to the next lane if you can.
Do not worry about it since they are merging.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the next lane if you can.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging may not see your motorcycle. Move to another lane if you can to give them safe space to merge.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Keep riding, it will likely stop on its own.
Brake quickly.
Close the throttle to slow down.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make wobbling worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down by closing the throttle gradually, lean forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as possible.

questions.question: When being passed, what is NOT a hazard?

options.text: Extended mirrors.
Objects thrown from other vehicles.
Wind blasts.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors, wind gusts, and objects thrown from the vehicle. Headlights are not a hazard when being passed.

questions.question: What should a proper lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help you set up for turns.
Provide an escape route.
Help you avoid wind blasts.
Put you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid blind spots, wind blasts, and hazards. It should give you an escape route and discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: How should a motorcyclist's following distance change?

options.text: It should always stay the same.
It should change based on road and traffic conditions.
It is not necessary in most situations.
It should be kept small to keep traffic moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should change based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see ahead clearly, or if traffic is heavy. More space is needed when your motorcycle takes longer to stop.

questions.question: What does a shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It protects your face in a crash.
It only protects you from dirt.
It does not protect as well as goggles.
You should not use it with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. It also protects you from dirt, dust, bugs, rain, and pebbles. Goggles only protect your eyes.

questions.question: What does an experienced rider do?

options.text: Changes lane position as conditions change.
Stays in one spot in the lane at all times.
Weaves back and forth to be more visible.
Always rides on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes lane position as conditions change.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has three lane position options. An experienced rider chooses the safest position based on road and traffic conditions at that moment.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position yourself?

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver already sees you.
Ride on the far left side of the lane.
Ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When riding behind a car, position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Riding in the center of the lane works best. The driver is most likely to notice you there.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake?

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly.
Use it only on slippery roads.
It is not as strong as the rear brake.
It is safe to use if you use it properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use if you use it properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It is safe to use it as long as you use it the right way.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Staying alert.
Spotting hazards and deciding which ones to address first.
Riding without a headlight.
Keeping space between you and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay alert and ready to react. Spot hazards and decide which ones to handle first. Always use your headlight to be more visible. Keep enough space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's total braking power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It supplies at least three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.
